Yikes, forgot to remove this pr from my local chain..... sorry.

We should run our Redfish Validator as part of CI. We don't. Compute resources are one of the things holding us back. 
We should have more testing to make sure endpoints aren't broken. We don't. Getting developers to buy into Unit testing, etc, has been a struggle.  

So we require some manual testing for each commit. Janet pointed out how an earlier patchset of this commit was broken (missing the route).. Since this is a refactor, verifying the output matches what was there before is a reasonable test. That is the kind of testing we expect with each commit.

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/efe29ab5ffd86b01d4848b470a14e29c54ecae43/docs/TESTING.md?plain=1#L4

That said, this is unlikely to break anything, and I would be okay with it going without the testing above. However, this is a complex enough change that I would really like to see some testing... And for the future, I really want to see testing on changes like this.

I can break up this change into smaller chunks, if you want, but I dont have the facilities to run this code on real hardware with proper configuration to run the validator against it. I just dont have the hardware and it's tiring to build custom qemu targets and em configs together for every other ressource node to test.

I am okay here, but for the future, we really require testing for this sort of change. I know this creates a higher barrier to contributions, but unless we get more resources at the project level, I don't see a better solution.

>  if you want, but I dont have the facilities to run this code on real hardware with proper configuration to run the validator against it.

I would highly recommend coming up with a solution.  Like Gunnar says, this patch is pretty easy to verify correctness based on a code review, but presumably refactoring isn't the scope of what you wanted to do with openbmc/bmcweb, so at some point, you'll need those qemu targets.  If you're on discord, I'm happy to help show you how I operate for most changes in qemu, which really isn't too bad to set up.

FWIW, you're welcome to use one of the two qemu targets I use upstream (nvidia-gb200-nvl72-bmc or s7106) as those models already exist and have been upstreamed.

This whole function has been superceeded with:

and
